proposals.expected_failure_mode: If true admissions lag is closer to 2 weeks, forecasts may peak early and under-represent the rising limb; may show mild split-to-split timing bias.
proposals.rationale: Primary candidate aligned with prior best spec; 1-week lag is a parsimonious way to map latent incidence proxy to hospitalization-rate reporting while minimizing phase drift risk and supporting stability across rolling splits.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Risk of over-lagging in some seasons/splits leading to late peaks and inflated tail; can increase instability if peak timing varies across splits.
proposals.rationale: Second core candidate to address observed delay sensitivity; 2-week lag can better align hospitalization timing without adding compartments, and may reduce peak misalignment for moderate-peakiness series.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Potential identifiability/over-flexibility: can fit noise or shift effective generation time, causing occasional split-specific phase drift and higher rolling variability.
proposals.rationale: Controlled exploration of fractional dynamics under the recommended constraint (fractional only with delay 1–2); may capture heterogeneous mixing/memory effects while keeping lag short to preserve timing stability.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Compounded timing uncertainty (fractional memory + longer lag) may over-smooth or delay peaks, increasing split-to-split variability and degrading stability if true lag is shorter.
proposals.rationale: Fractional + 2-week lag tests whether added flexibility improves robustness when admissions lag is longer; still within constrained search and avoids adding explicit H state per guidance.
